result.title: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? Working Conditions and the Limits of Occupational AI Exposure
result.summary: Automation is often justified as relief from dull, dirty, and dangerous work. I examine how these conditions relate to occupational AI exposure using 21 O*NET items across 754 US occupations. Higher exposure is associated with lower condition scores under a large language model (LLM) measure and AI Occupational Exposure (AIOE), with equal occupation weights and employment weights. Adjustment for physical demands, required education, training and experience, and wages reduces the composite association. The adjusted confidence intervals include zero for LLM exposure and remain below zero for AIOE. Separating repetition from restricted discretion also changes what the combined Dull score conveys. These comparisons show how item groupings and occupational characteristics shape the interpretation of exposure estimates. Occupational profiles offer a starting point for selecting contrasting research settings. Establishing desired automation or realized relief requires evidence about workers' preferences and specific interventions.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用 O*NET 的 21 个条目考察 754 个美国职业的「枯燥、肮脏、危险」工作条件与职业 AI 暴露度指标之间的关系，并分析条目分组与职业特征如何影响暴露度估计的解释。
AI.relevance_reason: 属劳动经济学层面的职业 AI 暴露度统计分析，不涉及模型内部表示、推理状态生成、视觉证据使用或训练监督，与 LVR/VLM 推理主线无实质联系，也无可借鉴的具体方法线索。
